## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, and early historical reports on the war and on the believers' reaction. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the Byzantines, the Persians and the dating of the defeat and the victory.
- The vowel reading of the verbs in 30:2-3 (defeated, will be victorious) is disputed in the readings tradition; a scholar of qira'at should decide how the page words it. The draft follows the common reading.
- The phrase 'on that day the believers will rejoice' (30:4-5) is rendered closely and left open as to its cause.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. Defeated, and will be victorious  (`#defeated-and-will-win`)

Cited ayat: 30:2-7

> **30:2** غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ
>
> **30:3** فِىٓ أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ
>
> **30:4** فِى بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ ٱلْأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِنۢ بَعْدُ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
>
> **30:5** بِنَصْرِ ٱللَّهِ يَنصُرُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
>
> **30:6** وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
>
> **30:7** يَعْلَمُونَ ظَٰهِرًا مِّنَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ هُمْ غَٰفِلُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (30:2-4): The Rum have been defeated, in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will themselves be victorious, in several years.

**c2** (30:4-5): The command belongs to God before and after; on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help.

**c3** (30:5): God helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

**c4** (30:6): It is the promise of God; God does not break His promise, but most people do not know.

**c5** (30:7): They know an outward part of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that the Rum have been defeated in the nearest land and will be victorious after their defeat, in several years [c1]. They add that the command belongs to God before and after, and that God does not break His promise [c2][c4].

### Complete story

The Rum have been defeated, in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will themselves be victorious, in several years [c1]. The command belongs to God before and after; on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help [c2].

God helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful [c3]. It is the promise of God; God does not break His promise, but most people do not know [c4]. They know an outward part of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter [c5].

### Deep study

The ayat speak of the past and of the future: a defeat that has happened and a victory that will follow it [c1]. The Arabic for nearest land can also be read as the lowest land, and the draft keeps it open [c1]. The final ayat turn from the event to people's knowledge, saying they know the outward part of this life and are heedless of the Hereafter [c4][c5].

### Kids mode

The ayat say that the Rum had been defeated but would win after some years [c1]. They say that God keeps His promise, though most people do not know it [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places an event under God's command, before and after it [c2]. Another is that it sets the outward knowledge of this life beside heedlessness of the Hereafter [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which battle or war is meant, who defeated the Rum, where the nearest land was, or when the defeat happened.
- Not established: how many years several covers, or in what event the victory came; the ayat give only several years.
- Not established: what the believers rejoiced at beyond God's help, or what the connection of the believers to the Rum was.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the Rum with the Byzantines, of their opponents with the Persians, and the places and years of the war.
